aions_core/agi_learning.py.why: It mines finished conversations for patterns and gaps to improve over time, rather than grading any single answer.

aions_core/memory_graph_engine.py.why: It is the map of how stored concepts refer to each other, kept in its own JSON file, not the ranking of retrieved passages.

aions_core/server/cbms_direct_server.py.why: It is the listening front door on port 9000 that routes a question through math, chit-chat, memory and web, not any one of those components.

aions_core/server/conversation_enhancer..why: It only reshapes tone and phrasing of an already-settled reply, never judging whether the facts are supported.

aions_core/server/conversation_memory.py.why: Its point is conversational continuity across turns, with chunk writing only a side effect of rolling up summaries.

aions_core/tools/bench_runner.py.why: It fires the same queries fifty times to time p50/p95 of the live service, which is speed measurement rather than answer correctness.

aions_core/tools/gsm8k_quick.py.why: It benchmarks accuracy and latency of the running service on a standard maths set, not the design of any refusal or quality rule.

aions_core/tools/query_db.py.why: It interrogates the drive-scan database to report which folders hold the most files, a survey job rather than chunk bookkeeping itself.

control_plane/__init__.py.why: It is the package marker for the control plane coordination layer, so it belongs with the command centre and not with any single skill.

control_plane/agents/agent_schema.py.why: It pins down which skills a role may use and its risk ceiling, fail-closed, which is permission shape rather than day-to-day skill running.

scripts/catalog_e_treasures.py.why: It inventories data and backup folders across drives by file count and gigabytes, a disk survey rather than manifest upkeep.

scripts/chatgpt_extractor.py.why: It recovers conversations out of another application's cache into local files, which is intake of outside text, not scanning code on disk.

scripts/demo_skill_live.py.why: It is a runnable showcase proving recipe reuse end to end, not the registry and executor machinery it calls into.

scripts/operator_profile_load.py.why: It loads the human owner's identity and preferences file, which is about the operator rather than environment paths or secrets.

scripts/vault/seal_secret.py.why: It locks API keys into a Windows-user-bound vault, which is credential protection, not permission checks on agent actions.

aions_core/aions_smart_guardrail.py.why: Its output is either evidence or an explicit refusal, so the point is not inventing answers rather than ranking the best passage.

aions_core/cbms_curve_machine.py.why: It declares kernels and composes them into retrieval, reasoning and backprop training graphs, which is thinking machinery rather than the day-to-day skill library.

aions_core/server/cbms_unified_server.py.why: It is the assembled chat endpoint wiring memory, facts, web and math together, not any single retrieval or wording component.

aions_core/server/esperanto_bridge.py.why: It rewrites Polish and English into a neutral middle language for symbolic indexing, the encoding scheme itself rather than the search that uses it.

aions_core/server/math_solver.py.why: It is the arithmetic and word-problem solver the chat front door tries first, not a reasoning-and-learning component.

aions_core/tools/web_crawler_import.py.why: It walks websites and files the sentences as facts with search keys, which is intake, not the later searching over them.

aions_core/verify_llama_cpp.py.why: It smoke-tests that the local model runtime library is installed, which is model machinery rather than general environment setup.

control_plane/llm/__init__.py.why: It documents the fast local model server channel and its fallback, so it sits with model loading and calling, not with plan dispatch.

control_plane/node_dispatch.py.why: It picks between running a step here or on a remote node, which is fleet routing rather than whether the action is permitted.

control_plane/orchestrator_loop.py.why: It is the top-level loop chaining mouth, retrieval gate and memory into one grounded answer, not one of those retrieval parts on its own.

control_plane/skills/executor.py.why: It chains skills and passes outputs forward, calling the gate rather than being the permission rules itself.

control_plane/skills/mcp_bridge.py.why: It is the bridge offering the skill registry and recipes to outside tool clients, with hot rediscovery of skills as its main concern.

mcpServers/VS_CODE_MCP_CODEX/src/desktop.why: It actually drives screen, keyboard and windows across Windows and Linux, not the protocol layer that publishes those abilities.

scripts/test_control_plane.py.why: It exercises plan storage, step execution and a remote node's API, verifying the job pipeline rather than demonstrating desktop work.

scripts/test_forge.py.why: It walks a new ability from request through build to promotion into the live registry, which is the approval pipeline rather than everyday skill use.
